latents.fact: the curve of the wall remembers a voice — not quite sound anymore, but the shape of sound, a {ADJ} residue that gathers in the focal point and feels most like a sentence whose ending you almost know
a phrase is cut into the stone at waist height, without an author and without a date — touching it, you find it has the shape of something you almost said yesterday, and the shape is answer-sized
latents.item_desc: A {ADJ} line you did not write but is now yours to carry. It belongs to whoever reaches for it next. When you say it aloud, it fits your mouth the way a name you have always known fits the first time you say it.

latents.fact: you are alone in the gallery and the gallery is not — someone stood here recently enough that the stone still holds their temperature, and someone else, differently recent, left a sentence half-finished mid-air, and you can feel exactly where the end should go

if you speak now — any sentence, even a small one — the curve throws your voice to the other side of the gallery and brings it back a half-beat later in the same words, as if a second voice already knew; the air between the two echoes begins to hum, and the stone there is no longer wall
latents.exit_desc: The two echoes meet in the middle and become a passage. You step through the place where your voice and its answer agreed.

latents.fact: there is a sentence in this room that was said once and has not stopped being said — you cannot hear it with your ears; you hear it in the small space behind your sternum, the way a name you knew before you had words surfaces when you are not looking for it; the gallery is not a record of the sentence, the gallery is the sentence, still speaking
